key_insight: An out-of-plane oscillating electric field can drive quasi-2D AgCrSe2 into a low-temperature nonequilibrium superionic state by inducing dynamic Ag+ disorder and fast in-plane transport far below its equilibrium transition temperature.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a timescale-matched field-driven strategy to turn on high ionic conductivity in solid electrolytes at much lower temperatures than conventional superionic transitions, potentially aiding low-temperature devices.
method: Apply an out-of-plane oscillating electric field to quasi-2D AgCrSe2
Track Ag+ occupation, sublattice switching, and ionic conductivity versus frequency, temperature, and field amplitude
evidence_signal: At 300 K, the simulations report activated in-plane Ag+ transport with ionic conductivity reaching about 1.7 S/cm, with distinct frequency-dependent regimes from switching to dynamic disorder to weak-response ordering.
watch_item: The mechanism depends on precise matching between driving frequency, field amplitude, and Ag-sublattice response time, so practical implementation may be sensitive to material quality, heating, and device-scale field delivery.
paper_title: Out-of-Plane Oscillating Electric Fields Unlock Low-Temperature Nonequilibrium Superionicity in Quasi-Two-Dimensional AgCrSe2
